categoryRules.description: Side sleepers generally benefit from a softer, more contouring surface that cushions the shoulder and hip.
A firmer sleep surface tends to create more pressure at the shoulder and hip for side sleepers.
Shoppers focused on pressure-point relief benefit from softer, contouring foam or hybrid comfort layers.
Stomach sleepers need enough firmness to avoid excess sinkage at the hips, which also limits uneven pressure.
Heavier back sleepers need a firmer, higher-support core to keep the spine aligned rather than sinking at the hips.
A softer mattress may not provide enough lift for a heavier back sleeper, risking spinal misalignment.
Stomach sleepers benefit from a firm, supportive core to prevent the hips from dropping out of alignment.
A soft mattress can let a stomach sleeper's hips sink too far, straining the lower back.
Zoned support layers target extra reinforcement under the lumbar region, which helps shoppers focused on back alignment.
Hot sleepers see the largest benefit from mattresses with high measured airflow ratings.
Low-airflow constructions tend to trap body heat, which is a poor match for a hot sleeper.
Dense all-foam constructions without cooling features are more likely to retain body heat overnight.
Sleepers who run cold often prefer a warmer, heat-retaining surface rather than a high-airflow design.
Couples and shared beds benefit substantially from strong motion isolation to avoid sleep disruption.
Highly motion-sensitive sleepers are especially affected by mattresses with poor motion isolation, such as traditional innerspring designs.
Reinforced perimeter edges give couples more usable sleep surface across the whole bed.
Without a reinforced perimeter, shared beds tend to feel like they lose usable surface area near the edges.
Combination sleepers who change positions frequently benefit from a responsive surface that doesn't trap movement.
A slow-responding, deep-contouring surface can make it harder for combination sleepers to reposition.
Heavier sleepers hold up best on constructions with a demonstrated low long-term sag risk.
Higher body weight accelerates body-impression formation on constructions with elevated sag risk.

riskRules.label: Support may be insufficient for your profile
riskRules.rationale: Your profile combines a heavier weight band with a back or stomach sleep position, which typically needs a firmer, higher-support core than this mattress provides.
riskRules.mitigation: Consider a firmer option (firmness 7+) with a reinforced or zoned support core, or ask the retailer about a firmer flip side if this model offers one.

riskRules.label: Firmness/support mismatch for stomach sleeping
riskRules.rationale: Stomach sleepers on a softer mattress often experience the hips sinking out of alignment with the shoulders, which can strain the lower back.
riskRules.mitigation: Look for a firmness rating of 7 or higher, or place a firm topper on this mattress to reduce hip sinkage.

riskRules.label: Heat retention likelihood
riskRules.rationale: This mattress's dense foam construction is more prone to trapping body heat, which may be uncomfortable for a self-reported hot sleeper.
riskRules.mitigation: Consider a breathable mattress protector, moisture-wicking sheets, or a model with active cooling features like gel infusion or coil airflow channels.

riskRules.label: Lower airflow configuration
riskRules.rationale: This mattress's measured airflow rating is on the lower end, which can make heat buildup more noticeable for a hot sleeper.
riskRules.mitigation: Look for models with an airflow rating above 70, or pair this mattress with a cooling mattress topper.

riskRules.label: Weaker edge support for a shared bed
riskRules.rationale: This mattress's edge support rating is below average, which can reduce usable sleep surface for two people sharing the bed.
riskRules.mitigation: Consider a model with a reinforced perimeter, or use bed rails to compensate for edge compression.

riskRules.label: No reinforced perimeter
riskRules.rationale: This mattress does not use a reinforced perimeter, so edge compression may be more noticeable over time in a shared bed.
riskRules.mitigation: This is a minor tradeoff if you mostly sleep toward the center of the bed; otherwise prioritize a reinforced-edge model.

riskRules.label: Sag/durability risk for your weight band
riskRules.rationale: This construction has a higher measured sag-risk rating, and heavier body weight tends to accelerate body-impression formation over time.
riskRules.mitigation: Consider a model with reinforced support layers and a sag-risk rating below 40, and rotate the mattress regularly to distribute wear.

riskRules.label: Foam durability risk at higher body weight
riskRules.rationale: All-foam constructions without a reinforced support core can compress unevenly under higher, sustained body weight.
riskRules.mitigation: A hybrid with a pocketed-coil or zoned support core will typically hold up better at this weight band.

riskRules.label: Firmer than your stated preference
riskRules.rationale: You told us you prefer a soft or medium-soft feel, but this mattress's firmness rating is on the firm end of the scale.
riskRules.mitigation: If a softer feel matters most, look for a mattress rated 4 or below on our firmness scale, or ask about a plush comfort-layer option.

riskRules.label: Softer than your stated preference
riskRules.rationale: You told us you prefer a medium-firm or firm feel, but this mattress's firmness rating is on the soft end of the scale.
riskRules.mitigation: If firmer support matters most, look for a mattress rated 7 or higher on our firmness scale.
